lines.en: I hate Christmas.
And despite not knowing much about my previous life or my opinions on the holiday when I was younger, I have a feeling I hated it then, too.
Sure, the cold is nice. But are the bright lights and all the decorations really necessary?
And it’s not even always cold on Christmas to begin with, so the one good thing I was able to think up off the top of my head has already gone out the window.
But maybe, in some sort of Christmas miracle like you’d see in those old American movies-
I’ll have a good time this year.
I mean, the girls in my class are nowhere near my family (Except for Ami and kind of Ayane, I guess)...
But at least I’ll be surrounded by people who I don’t inherently despise instead of some drunk [uncle] or dying grandmother.
It’s kind of nice having dodged such a dangerous bullet in the form of this party, though.
Considering that Christmas in Japan is more of a time for couples to spend together and I am involved in a number of illicit relationships right now...
Not having to choose which girl takes up most of my time today is definitely a good thing.
I’m going to need a bigger Christmas miracle than just that, though, if I’m going to be able to ignore all of the joy I expect to endure today.
The day gets off to an inopportune start with none of that fluffy, white stuff coming out of the sky.
Thankfully, the lingering cold from last night’s snowfall sticks around just like the powder that came with it-
And I crunch my way down the street with Ami, Ayane, and Maya as we head toward the store to buy some things for tonight.
Even though everyone passed out extremely early last night, we were able to salvage most of the stuff I bought with Maya- save a few pints of ice cream that never made it into the freezer.
Again, going to need a bigger Christmas miracle than just this to get through the day without a frown consuming my face- reddish and dry from being beaten by the wind.
Another bad thing happens before we’re able to make it to the hotel.
Apparently, the girls wanted to go look at Christmas trees for my house because that is a thing I’m supposed to buy, I guess.
Damn [niece] and her friends can’t even be Japanese correctly. Why are we going all out for a holiday that’s supposed to be centered around sex and fried chicken?
This is stupid.
I hate Christmas.
I really do.
: Sensei! I want this one!
: No.
: Oh! What about this one?!
: That one wouldn’t even fit in our house.
: How about this?
I turn around to find Maya holding up a twig that fell out of a tree and, for the first time probably ever, I think she’s actually kind of funny.
Also, twigs are cheap, so I easily decide on our Christmas tree for the-
: If you even think about humoring her I’m gonna log into your Amazon account and order like four trees in the middle of the night.
: But you don’t know my-
: I do. It’s Boobies123. You use the same password for everything.
: He does?
: So I could log in to his LINE account and see if he’s been sending naughty pics to anyone else in class?
: Why did you add an ‘else’ to that? I haven’t sent any to you and that insinuates I have.
: You’re disgusting.
: Are you not listening? I just said I never sent anything like that.
I hate Christmas.
So no Christmas tree was purchased today.
I like Ami, though. And I’m weak around cute girls, so I’ll probably wind up caving and buying one sooner or later.
But for now, there are other, more important matters to attend to.
We’re supposed to meet everyone at some hotel in the busiest part of town- kind of halfway between where we go to[school] and where Futaba’s friend with the glasses goes.
And eventually, we get there.
I’m greeted by a peculiar sight once we enter, though.
: Karin?
: Uhh, hey! Fancy meeting you in the place that we’re inside of right now. Which is a hotel.
: Thanks. I had no idea.
: Do you work here?
: Umm...no. But the girl at the desk was having some sort of emergency and I kind of volunteered to just...take her place.
: But I have no idea what I’m doing and I don’t think I’m even technically allowed to be back here.
: And now you’re here and I’m even more nervous and just hoping that you don’t need to check in or- yeah.
: Oh. Well I do.
: But I can wait until the other person gets back.
: There’s no need for that, Sensei. Makoto handled it a little while ago.
: Oh. You guys were here too? I didn’t even see you.
: Oh, okay. I guess I’ll just keep standing here and talking to myself, then...
: Are you ready for a large man to climb down your chimney and eat all of your food?
: I would be if Santa Claus ex-
: STOP!
: What’s your problem?
: I have no problem since Santa Claus exists and everyone believes in him.
: Obviously. Why would anyone doubt the existence of a man who defies the laws of physics by inserting himself into spaces he clearly is not supposed to fit.
And here I was thinking Santa and I had nothing in common.
: Anyway, what are you guys up to?
: If Makoto checked in, shouldn’t you be up in the room?
: Yes, but...Molly has been in the middle of something since we got here and is refusing to go up to the room until she’s done.
: Well what’s she doing? Playing a game?
: GIVE...ME...MY...GEO...BOY!
: I don’t know what that means.
: Just pretend you do. It gets me by.
: It really doesn’t, though, Tsuneyo.
: Ah-
: I’m surprised you stuck around, Futaba. I figured you’d be with Rin or something.
: Yeah, well...I kind of got absorbed in Molly’s efforts and have been cheering her on from the sidelines.
: I need you here so I can absorb your energy.
: And there’s that. She needs to...absorb my energy.
: Right...
I turn around to tell Ami and the others that we should probably be heading upstairs to thank Makoto, but...
: Where did my [niece] go?
: If you’re talking about the girl with the nice legs, she went upstairs with two others as soon as you walked in.
: Are you really going to address Ami as “the girl with the nice legs” every time she’s brought up?
: Until proven otherwise, probably.
: So...if you’re all down here and everyone else is up there, who’s left? Are we missing anybody?
: Are you worried that someone may have gotten lost on the way? That’s awfully considerate of you.
: Well, the roads looked pretty bad, so knowing everyone is still alive would be nice.
: Hah!
: Ohmygodohmygodohmygodohmygodohmygodohmygodohmygodohmygod!
: TAKE THAT, WORLD!
: YOU THOUGHT YOU COULD RUIN CHRISTMAS FOR ME, BUT I HAVE THE POWER OF TWO MONTHS PART TIME BARISTA MONEY TO BURN IN PROTEST!
: FUCK YEAH!
: Congrats on doing whatever you were trying to do, Molly.
: Oh! Hello, Sir!
: Merry Christmas.
: For your present, may I inform you that there are two lovely ladies behind you who seem to want your attention?
: And with them, it looks like everyone is finally here.
: Wait, who’s behind me?
: Wow. You know it’s a special night when Yumi graces us with her presence.
: Fuck off, dickhead.
: Merry Christmas, Sensei~
: Yumi’s broke so I made her do this one thing for me so she wouldn’t have to get me a present this year.
: It’s not like I would have even gotten you one anyway. Christmas is stupid. It’s just an excuse for companies to make more money and shit.
: Hey, it looks like we might finally agree on something.
: Huh? Really?
: Wait a minute, don’t tell me you’re just as anti-Christmas as Yumi, Sensei.
: To be totally honest, I’m really not a fan.
: I implore you to look over my outfit a few more times and then reconsider.
: There are only so many days a year I can wear this, you know.
: Yup. And it only took you like two hours to get ready.
: Well shit, Yumi! Sorry for taking so long in my bathroom while you laid on my bed watching my TV for those two hours!
: That must have been really hard on you!
: It’s whatever. Just don’t come cryin’ to me when you get a cold and have to sleep in the dorm room instead of your house every night.
: You were complainin’ the whole way here about how cold you were and shit and I can’t blame you since you’re dressed like a fuckin’ holly-jolly ho-bag.
: You don’t think I look like a holly-jolly ho-bag, do you, Sensei?
I think you look great
: Of course not. I think you’re adorable.
: Hah...here we go.
: Hotel room is upstairs. If you two are gonna get all weird with each other, at least be respectful enough to not do it in the fuckin’ lobby.
: You really think so?!
: Of course. I can’t imagine many other girls being able to pull that off without looking a little too...promiscuous.
: Isn’t that basically saying she just looks slutty but like, not as slutty?
: Shut up, Yumi. You’re just jealous that I was complimented and you weren’t.
: Yeah, that really doesn’t matter at all to me...
Chika’s affection has increased to [chika_love]!
Yumi’s got a point
: I hate to break it to you, Chika...But I think Yumi’s right.
: You do?...
: You...do?
: Yeah.
: I mean, it’s one thing to wear something like that in private, but walking into a hotel lobby dressed that way is kind of...inappropriate.
: Is it...really that bad?
: I knew it was showing a bit of skin but I really didn’t think it was that much of an issue.
: Especially with like, zero boys around.
: I just...wanted you to think I was pretty and stuff.
Yumi’s affection has increased to [yumi_love]!
: Either way, I think you’re both adorable tonight.
: The new hairstyles are a nice change of pace.
: Oh, suck my dick. I look the same as always.
: On behalf of both of us, thank you~
: I like your new shirt, Sensei. It looks slightly thicker.
: Thank you, Chika. I was wondering when someone would realize that.
Everyone remaining in the lobby slowly but surely disperses until they all wind up in the hotel room.
And, by association, I end up there as well.
: Well, I’ll be. You are back to normal after all.
: Back to normal? Which one of us are you talking about, exactly?
: You. Last time I saw you I pushed you up against a locker.
: Wha-?!
: I don’t know what sort of strange fantasies you have about us, but I can assure you that this locker-pushing never happened!
: And anything that did actually happen would best not be discussed here!
: Yeah, yeah. I get it. I was just messing around with you.
Obviously, I wasn’t.
But it looks like the reset somehow...fixed Makoto- which is strange given that Maya claimed to have not known anything was different about her.
But, then again, I wouldn’t put it past Maya to lie about something like that and just go behind my back and fix things on her own.
She seems a little too independent for her own good, sometimes.
: More importantly, Sensei. Do you notice anything a little...different about my best friend here?
: Different? You mean Miku’s hair?
: Yeah. It was the first thing I noticed when I came in here.
: Mm...Don’t stare at me. It feels weird.
: As you can see, she’s very embarrassed.
: And I’m not saying you’d be able to find any flaws in her makeover but, if you do, please keep them to yourself as I am the one who cut her hair this morning.
: It’s not...weird...right?
: Cause I was really tired this mornin’ and kinda just agreed to let Makoto do her thing to make me look more girly and stuff but like...
: I didn’t know she was gonna chop so much off. I keep lookin’ in the mirror and bein’ like “Woah who the heck is that?”
: And now I’m really self-conscience or whatever the word is.
: Self-conscious. And you have no reason to be. You look adorable.
: And you were complaining about your hair getting longer anyway. So now it’ll stay out of your eyes when you’re playing soccer.
: I know...
: I’ve just gotta get used to it, I guess.
: I was worried people were gonna think I was tryin’ too hard to...not be Miku anymore.
: I’m sure you’ll remain Miku no matter how you style your hair.
: I think you’re cute no matter what.
: Okay, now let’s not get too complimentary, Sensei. Please remember that Miku is one of your students and that I will report anything unsavory you have to say about her.
Says the girl who I deflowered at a Halloween party.
: Report whatever you want. I’ve got some other people to greet anyway.
: Yes, yes. I completely understand.
: But do know that this is a relatively small hotel room and I’m sure to hear it if you decide to hit on any of these wonderful [young_girls].
: Thanks, Makoto. I’ll keep that in mind.
: Do you feel at all strange knowing that we’re sitting on a bed with two swans kissing behind us?
: I was hoping you weren’t going to mention that.
: Why are those even here?
: What kind of hotel room is this?
: Well, you know...Christmas is a popular day for dates, so...
: Maybe the hotel got the...wrong idea or something?
: Or they watched fourteen girls come up here with one man and are going to tell this story for the rest of their lives.
: Yeah...or that.
: They should have brought up more swans.
: Merry Christmas, Ami.
: Merry Christmas, Maya...
: Hey, you two. How are you doing?
: Hi, Sensei...
: M...Merry Christmas...
: What’s going on with Rin?
: Oh, she’s texting a friend of hers...
: I’m just...standing here since Ayane is busy and...I don’t really talk to anyone else.
: But now you’re here, so...
: I’m going to talk to you...if that’s okay.
: Of course it’s okay. It’s not like Rin to ignore me, though.
: Huh? Rin? That’s me.
: I heard my name.
: Oh! Sensei! Merry Christmas!
: Merry Christmas. What’s this about talking to a friend?
: You know you’ve already got one friend beside you just...standing there, right?
: It’s okay...I’m used to being forgotten...
: Oh, crap! I’m sorry, Sana! I was just reading this one thing Otoha sent me and I got lost in thought.
: I’ll do better. Promise!
: Otoha? That name sounds familiar.
: She’s the girl we saw playing guitar in the park that one time.
: I wound up bumping into her again totally by accident and we exchanged numbers.
: You put some strange emphasis on “totally by accident” there.
: No idea what you’re talking about.
: But yeah, we’re friends now.
: But I hereby give you permission to confiscate my phone if I get too absorbed in it.
: Otoha’s cool, so she’ll understand.
: Duly noted.
: Otoha? That’s a name I’ve never heard before.
: Probs cause it’s a girl you’ve never met before.
: I bumped into her at some park near my old[school] with Futaba a while back.
: She’s this super talented musician and she’s crazy pretty and I’m definitely not becoming obsessed or whatever.
: It...sounds like you are...
: Okay, maybe just a little bit.
: But still, I hereby give you permission to confiscate my phone if I get too absorbed in it.
: Otoha’s cool, so she’ll understand.
: Duly noted.
: So, umm...Sensei...
: Did you...bring a present for your Secret Santa...person?
: Oooooh yeah, we’re supposed to leave ‘em near the door.
: Can you tell us who you got? As long as it’s not either of us, of course.
: You completely forgot, didn’t you?
: Yes, but in my defense, it’s less of me forgetting and more of me never finding out in the first place.
: I literally watched you pull a name out of a hat.
: That’s...not good...
: You’re the one who was keeping track of the names so...I don’t know who you can even ask...
: That does not sound like a thing I would ever do, but I’ve already thought up a solution.
: What is it? Gonna wait until everyone else exchanges gifts and then just keep an eye on who the one person to not get any is?
: Oh come on, even I wouldn’t stoop that low.
Fuck. She got me.
Maybe Maya will know?
She knew all about this get together so...maybe she’ll remember who I’m supposed to give a present to?
I’ll have to pull her aside when she’s not...on a swan-bed with my [niece].
Meanwhile...
